body: Yeah, we do; it's necessary for formats where the minor is something like `1a.2`; then for this sloppy state we still want to show something major-ish; with versions like that we're off in the weeds, but at least it gets us something. The versions library for Rust is a weeeee bit persnickety about version types -- assuming they're ints! hah! -- so this is a bit of flexibility I baked in.

The unfortunate reality of version parsing :upside_down_face: 
Just wanted to verify that this was in fact intentional :+1:

Yes, that library is the result of years of handling ridiculous version numbers in https://github.com/fosskers/aura :)

Happy to see the library being used elsewhere, please let me know if you have any issues.

> assuming they're ints!

The `Version` and `Mess` subtypes are much more permissive about what can appear in a particular position. Did you find something missing?

Thanks for stopping by and thanks **a lot** for providing us with a great library!

> Yes, that library is the result of years of handling ridiculous version numbers in [fosskers/aura](https://github.com/fosskers/aura) :)

> Happy to see the library being used elsewhere, please let me know if you have any issues.

Sure we'll let you know but luckily most of the versions we are dealing with are in fact semver conformant.

Also, that goes both ways, assuming that you are a Starship user? , let us know if there is anything we could do to make it even better ;)
